question: The transformer was introduced in 2017. How does that architecture relate to the chat models you use today?

options.text: It has been replaced by a newer architecture designed for chat
options.feedback: It feels as though something so much better must have replaced a 2017 design, but the lecture's point was the opposite: the architecture has not changed. What changed is how big it is and how much text it is trained on.

options.text: It survives only as the part of the model that handles grammar
options.feedback: The transformer is the whole model, not one component inside it. The pipeline you saw, from context to next token, is the transformer end to end.

options.text: It is the same architecture, scaled up
options.feedback: Today's models are the 2017 design made much bigger and trained on trillions of words instead of a million. That is why one pipeline diagram describes Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini alike.

options.text: It is the same architecture, retrained yearly on the same amount of text
options.feedback: The architecture is indeed the same, but the scale is not. The lecture stressed that training went from about a million words to trillions, and the models themselves grew along with it.
